blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, feedback becomes less a communication skill and more a leadership discipline. The question is not "how do I say this?" but "what kind of culture am I creating by how I give, receive and withhold feedback?" Senior leaders shape organisations more through the pattern of their feedback than through any strategy they publish.

Three principles separate good from great. First, feedback must be specific and timely — not saved for the next review, not buried in a long email. Second, it must be given about the work, never in a way that diminishes the person. Third, and most importantly, it must be welcomed upwards as fluently as it is given downwards. A senior leader who cannot hear feedback themselves quietly teaches the whole organisation that feedback is dangerous.

The best executives share one trait: they receive feedback more gracefully than almost anyone in the room. They thank the person, ask a clarifying question, and consider it visibly. That single habit, repeated over years, does more to build a high-feedback culture than any programme, training or policy ever could.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level feedback is best understood as…
items.why: "feedback becomes less a communication skill and more a leadership discipline."

items.q: Which set of qualities does the text say feedback must have?
options: Specific and timely, about the work
items.why: "feedback must be specific and timely… given about the work, never in a way that diminishes the person."

items.q: The text says a leader who cannot hear feedback themselves…
options: teaches the organisation that feedback is dangerous
will simply receive less of it over time
items.why: "quietly teaches the whole organisation that feedback is dangerous."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Receiving feedback gracefully is a leadership habit.
Feedback should be about the work, not the person.
How a leader receives feedback shapes the whole culture.
A polished strategy document matters more than the feedback a leader models.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que líderes moldam a organização mais pelo padrão de feedback do que por qualquer estratégia publicada.

items.q: The emphasis on welcoming feedback "upwards as fluently as it is given downwards" suggests that…
options: modelling openness matters more than issuing critique
the direction of feedback is irrelevant
only senior leaders should receive feedback
items.why: Inferência: o hábito de receber bem é apontado como o que mais constrói a cultura — mais do que dar feedback para baixo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie na sessão com o time executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. I want to talk about something that no strategy offsite ever fixes, and that is what happens in the room when someone challenges the CEO.

Here is what I have observed across this business. Your teams are watching, constantly, for one signal: is it safe to disagree with the person at the top? And they do not read the values on the wall to find out. They read your face the moment feedback comes upwards.

Last quarter, a junior analyst pushed back on a forecast in front of thirty people. The CEO paused, thanked her, and asked one clarifying question. That thirty-second exchange did more for our culture than the whole engagement survey. Within a week, three other teams told me they had started raising concerns earlier.

So my ask today is uncomfortable but simple. Do not focus on how skilfully you deliver criticism downwards. Focus on how gracefully you receive it upwards. If you want a high-feedback culture, you have to be the first person in the room to say, out loud, tell me what I am getting wrong — and mean it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Sophie, what are teams constantly watching for?
options: Whether the CEO delivers criticism skilfully
Whether it is safe to disagree with the person at the top
Whether the values are printed on the wall
Whether the strategy offsite produced results
items.why: "is it safe to disagree with the person at the top?"

items.q: What did the CEO do when the junior analyst pushed back?
options: Paused, thanked her, and asked a clarifying question
Asked her to raise it privately later
items.why: "The CEO paused, thanked her, and asked one clarifying question."

items.q: What does Sophie say teams read to judge whether disagreement is safe?
options: The leader's face when feedback comes upwards
items.why: "They read your face the moment feedback comes upwards."

items.q: Why does Sophie call her request "uncomfortable but simple"?
options: It requires more meetings than leaders expect
It cannot be measured by any survey
It asks leaders to invite criticism of themselves, not just give it
items.why: Inferência: o desconforto está em pedir para ouvir os próprios erros, invertendo o instinto de só dar feedback para baixo.

items.q: The anecdote about the analyst is used mainly to show that…
options: junior staff are usually right about forecasts
small visible moments shape culture more than formal programmes
surveys are the best measure of culture
items.why: Inferência: um gesto de trinta segundos fez mais pela cultura do que a pesquisa inteira — o exemplo prova o valor do momento visível.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Treating feedback as a leadership discipline means practising it deliberately, not by mood." Here, discipline means…
items.why: Discipline = disciplina: uma prática deliberada e consistente, não punição.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Managers who ___ praise until the annual review lose most of its impact."
items.why: Withhold = reter: segurar o elogio até a avaliação anual.

items.q: "Criticism that diminishes the person, rather than the work, erodes trust." To diminish someone is to…
options: make them feel smaller or lesser
items.why: To diminish = diminuir: fazer a pessoa se sentir menor, atacando a pessoa e não o trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She received the harsh feedback ___, thanking him before responding."
items.why: Gracefully = com elegância: receber a crítica com serenidade e agradecimento.

items.q: "The one trait the best leaders share is a hunger for feedback." A trait is…
items.why: Trait = traço: uma característica estável da pessoa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre feedback e liderança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The analyst pushed back on the forecast in front of the board." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — discordar de forma aberta.

items.q: "Leaders who ask for feedback but never follow through teach people to stop bothering." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim, agir sobre o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Praising the team publicly but reprimanding one person privately can backfire if it looks staged." To backfire means to…
options: produce the opposite of the intended effect
items.why: Backfire = sair pela culatra: produzir o efeito contrário ao desejado.

items.q: "A thirty-second exchange did more to move the needle on our culture than the whole survey." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Before we escalate, let's touch base with the regional heads to hear their view." To touch base means to…
items.why: Touch base = fazer um contato rápido para alinhar antes de seguir.
